Great game, it is still relevant after 10+ years, strong community. Cartoony style, enjoyable combat and customisation are one of the many reasons it was popular in first place. You can have fun just by playing, no matter are you winning or losing, this is game design others should strive for.
But there are some problems that need adressing. The most major is that it doesn't get a lot of attention from Valve in last years. When playing on official servers you will face the cheaters/bots. AND A LOAD OF THEM. Valve anticheat isn't working properly, and bots are flooding matches, and even when there is only one of them, it steals fun from both teams. I hope Valve will resolve this problem properly. Also being F2P hurts, you cannot chat, scream for help, limited item drops, and You can often be regarded as a bot by other players.
If Valve will do something about those problems, tf2 will be truly enjoyed by many new and veteran players alike.

This is a great game with an impressive market economy and a lovely community overall. 42/10 this game is the answer to life and everything.

The 9 classes - each with their distinct play styles, functions and quirks work- harmoniously together to lead to a very entertaining gaming experience. Yes, certain classes counter others almost too well (i.e. pyro > spy > sniper), but the game offers plenty of depth to explore and master! I'm only a couple thousand hours in, and I discover new tricks and eggs all the time.

My favorite part about this game is participating in the trading scene and economy. My best memories are working with other traders to make deals that were mutually beneficial and building my inventory to be worth some hundreds dollars. Many days, I could just relax and casually trade on casual maps while getting stab sprees as spy or landing market gardener crits.

As the community expands, all people are welcome.
Unless you're playing w+m1 pyro or with mini sentries on hightower, then you're just a scrub and should stop playing.
